question: How do the portfolio's valuations compare with public peers?
html:
The available data cannot yet compare BSP portfolio company valuations with public peers. The public comparables set reports growth, margins and revenue per employee, not trading multiples, and BSP entry and current valuations are not in the context. The data can show how each portfolio company's economics line up against peers, and where private-deal multiples sit.

What the data supports

  • Public peers are benchmarked on operations only. Their EBITDA is operating income plus D&A, unadjusted (Public comparables).
  • The only portfolio entry multiple is Frontline at about 12-15x, and that is an estimate (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Multiple evidence comes from bankers and press reports, not public trading data (ServiceOS evidence).

Peer benchmarks and multiple ranges

Portfolio companyPublic peer benchmarkMultiple reference pointsPremium (turns, est.)
Punctual ProsPeer median 14.4% operating margin, 15.1% EBITDA marginPKF 5-6x vs 10x+; Champions ~18.5x, Sila ~17x (press est.)1.0-2.5
CETElectrical/MEP revenue CAGR 16.8%; commercial electrical median 6.4% operating marginCapstone 6.8x typical vs 9.8x premium0.5-1.5
FrontlineOnshore professional services earn 3-9% operating margin (CBIZ $290k revenue per employee)Aventis MSP curve 5.2x-11.2x0.5-1.5
Thomas ScientificAvantor ~80% digital transactionsNo disclosed multiple premium0.5-1.0
BPIAgencies median +0.3% growth; WPP -8.1%PPHC ~8.4x floor vs 10-13x est. sponsor exit0.5-2.0
Fair HarborNot shown in the contextNot shown in the contextNot shown

Peer benchmarks are from the Public comparables file. Multiple reference points and premium ranges are from the ServiceOS evidence file.

How to read this

  • Frontline's estimated entry of about 12-15x already sits above the top of the Aventis MSP curve. Further multiple expansion there is harder to argue (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Punctual Pros has the widest potential premium. The 17-18.5x prints come from scale and membership density, not technology alone (ServiceOS evidence).
  • Residential peers are split into two groups. Installers grew only 1-1.5%, while faster growers leaned on non-residential work. Mid-teens EBITDA margin is the realistic mature target (Public comparables).
  • At Thomas Scientific, the exit case rests on EBITDA and leverage, not multiple (ServiceOS evidence).
  • The $12.7M agent-program value is an assumption-based estimate, not company data (Portfolio AI-agent plan).

Data needed to answer directly

  • EV/EBITDA for the 31 public peers, as of a common date.
  • BSP entry multiples and current LTM adjusted EBITDA for each portfolio company.
  • Portfolio company revenue, so revenue per employee can be computed. For example, Frontline has about 1,100 employees, but no revenue figure is in the context (BSP firm profile).

Next actions

  1. Pull trading multiples for the 31-peer set as of Oct 8, 2026, and add them to the Public comparables file.
  2. Compile entry multiples and LTM adjusted EBITDA for all six portfolio companies from fund reporting.
  3. Rebuild each company's margin and revenue-per-employee position against its peer median, adjusting both sides to the same EBITDA definition.
  4. Recheck the premium-turn ranges once real multiples are in. Start with Frontline, where the estimated entry multiple already exceeds the banker curve.
